title: Lav 4
hookLine: the fourth round: the mind at peace, the Lord found in ease (Suhi M4, ang 774)
last: AS THE WORD COMES · GUARDED · THE FRIEND IS HOME · DHARMA · FEARLESS · LONGING.

lines: A QUIET AFTER A LONG ROAD.
cards: Picture a couple fifty years in, at the kitchen table doing the crossword. Nobody's talking much. One reaches for the pen and the other has already slid it across.
There's nothing romantic about it, and yet it says more than a candlelit dinner could. Not the fireworks at the start, but a quiet that only comes after a long road.
The last round of the Sikh wedding ends in a word for exactly that kind of ease.

teach.h: ROUND FOUR: THE MIND AT REST.
teach.b: The fourth stanza of Guru Ram Das's laavan, on Ang seven seventy-four, says, in paraphrase: in the fourth round, the mind becomes calm, and the Lord is found.

The Lord is met in sahaj, in natural ease, and feels sweet to body and mind. The bride's heart blooms; she is joined with the Lord. And it ends: in the fourth round, Nanak says, the eternal Lord is found.
Sahaj means ease, balance, the natural state. Gurbani uses it again and again for the settled peace of someone who has met God: not a high, but level ground. So the four rounds trace a whole journey.
Duty in round one. Fear and ego washed away in round two. Longing in round three.
And in round four, rest. For the soul, that's union with God. For the couple, it's a picture of where a long marriage can arrive.

Another line in the Guru Granth Sahib, by Guru Amar Das on Ang seven eighty-eight, says husband and wife are not those who merely sit together; they are one light in two bodies. Many Sikhs think of that line at weddings.

When the fourth round ends, the couple bows and sits, and the ceremony closes with the Anand Sahib, the song of bliss, and Ardas. Then the karah prashad is shared, and the two are married. No ring has to change hands.
Four rounds of words, walked together, have done it.

how: At the Anand Karaj, the fourth lav is read and sung as the couple walks a last time around the Guru Granth Sahib; the ceremony then closes with verses of Anand Sahib, Ardas and karah prashad.

o: natural ease, the mind at rest
the bride's vow to her husband
a burst of joy at the wedding

games.q: the fourth round has been walked and the couple sits down. what comes next?
o: a fifth round for the families.
Anand Sahib, Ardas, and karah prashad shared.
games.why: the ceremony closes with the song of bliss, Ardas, and karah prashad. four rounds of words have married them.

practice: Walk the last slow clockwise round, or trace it with your hand, bringing no duty, fear or longing this time; just walk at whatever pace is easy, and let your breath set the speed.
Then sit and do nothing for a while: sahaj in miniature. If you pray, say Waheguru once, softly.

wordCard.voice: Sahaj, natural ease, balance: in the last round of the Sikh wedding, the mind grows calm, the Lord is met in it, and the journey of the four rounds is complete.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: natural ease, balance; the fourth round meets the Lord in sahaj.

carryVoice: Your line: round four: union. Not fireworks, but level ground. Day six hundred sixty-five, done.
